text:
incident-bot: PAGED: PagerDuty alert fired for service `inference-edge` — alert: `p99_latency_eu-west` exceeded threshold (500ms) for 10m. PD: https://pagerduty.example/INC-8241 · urgency: high · triggered_at: 2026-03-15T12:32:01Z

maria: Acked on-call page. I'm looking at dashboards now. @aj @sasha please chime if you see anything obvious.

aj: I'm on primary. pulling p99 heatmap — looks concentrated on /v1/rerank and /v1/embed routes in eu-west.

sasha: KV cache eviction rate spiked ~12:24Z in eu-west. Also seeing elevated sidecar queueing on hosts gw-eu-03/04.

leo: I saw a small rolling deployment at 12:18Z in the eu-west autoscaling group — could be correlated. Checking deploy history.

maria: copying quick checks: `kubectl get hpa -n inference eu-west-autoscaler` and `monitoring query`

aj: ran query — p99 over last 15m for eu-west: 820ms -> 730ms -> 650ms -> still high. error rate unchanged. So latency-only.

sasha: stack traces look like longer model decode times and KV cache misses. Tagging svc:rerank-v2 heavy.

maria: preliminary customer impact: approx 3-4% of total requests in eu-west see >500ms p99. No errors, so functionality intact but degraded UX.

devops-bot: note: autoscaler attempted scale at 12:20Z but throttled by quota. quota remaining: 0.3 units.

maria: mitigation options: 1) route traffic away from rerank-v2 to a compatible lower-latency variant; 2) temporarily increase concurrency/scale if quota freed; 3) evict stale KV cache keys; 4) rollback the 12:18 deploy if it's causal.

aj: I'm going to try routing ~30% of rerank traffic to `rw-rerank-fast-v1` as a canary fallback. Applying routing override now.

maria: +1. Also please enable auto-fallback so if the canary reaches error/latency thresholds it will shift more.

aj: `routing-tool apply --scope eu-west --route /v1/rerank=rw-rerank-fast-v1 --weight 30`

devops-bot: routing change queued. Applying to 12 nodes.

devops-bot: routing change applied (12/12 nodes updated) — rollout id r-20260315-0021.

aj: initial effect: p99 dropping from ~820ms -> ~480ms on canary path. Overall eu-west p99 moved from 780ms -> 520ms in last 60s.

leo: freed up some quota by temporarily pausing noncritical batch jobs. Requesting a short burst increase with infra.

irene: checking customer-facing queues — dark traffic shows improved latency on canary. I'll open an incident ticket to notify support teams. Ticket: CO-6124.

sasha: additional observation: KV cache miss ratio still elevated for keys with >7d TTL. Running targeted eviction on the largest 10 keys in gw-eu-03.

maria: go ahead with eviction, but throttle evictions to avoid stampede. Use `cachectl evict --targets key1,key2 ... --rate 5/s`.

aj: evictions started. Applying 5/s throttling.

maria: also enabling route-level concurrency cap to protect the rerank service: `max_concurrency=60` for rerank-v2.

devops-bot: concurrency cap applied on 10 nodes.

aj: p99 now at 310ms eu-west after routing + evictions + concurrency cap. Good signal trending.

maria: Ok — we have a stable partial mitigation. Next steps: continue monitoring for 15m, decide on rollback if latency re-spikes. Document timeline and mitigation actions for postmortem.

leo: follow-up: I confirmed the 12:18 deploy touched a batching optimization which could increase tail latency under high cache-miss rates. I'll prepare a rollback PR standby.

irene: I've created support notification with CO-6124 and included initial impact estimate (3-4% requests, p99 up to 820ms, no consumer errors). Support will notify affected accounts with SLA sensitivity.

sasha: curious: autopager suppression flags were modified earlier — looks like PD suppression threshold set to 550ms which caused repeated pages. We should tune suppression to avoid pager loops on noisy transient spikes.

maria: Agree. For now we'll keep autopager enabled but increase suppression window to 12m for p99 alerts to reduce noisy-firing.

aj: applying suppression change: `incidentctl suppress --alert p99_latency_eu-west --window 12m`

incident-bot: suppression updated for `p99_latency_eu-west` (12m).

maria: handing off to aj for continued monitoring and follow-ups. I will update the incident doc and start the postmortem outline.

aj: Taking handoff at 12:40Z. I'll watch for re-escalation and coordinate rollback if we see regression.

irene: noted. Postmortem owner: maria, action owner for rollback: leo, follow-up support comms: irene.

maria: thanks all. Will reconvene in ~45m for a short triage sync. :white_check_mark:

aj: thanks — closing this on-call thread unless side effects appear.

incident-bot: NOTE: PagerDuty incident INC-8241 remains open and assigned to `inference-oncall`.

maria: adding final summary to incident doc: "12:32Z p99_latency_eu-west spike caused by KV cache miss storm + recent batching deploy; mitigated by routing to low-latency model variant, targeted KV evictions, concurrency caps, and brief quota reallocation. Customer impact limited to latency degradation for ~3-4% of EU requests. Postmortem in progress."

aj: logging metrics snapshot and screenshots to the incident doc: https://redwood.internal/incident/INC-8241

maria: handoff complete.
